**Ruling: B in this repo, D relayed cross-repo, A rejected, C stays roadmap.** This follows the card's own lean and the non-tolerant-consumer principle: (B) `parseLiteral`'s tail `return s` gains a dev-mode diagnostic when the input looks like a path (contains `.` or matches identifier grammar) — "right side treated as a string literal", zero semantic change, turning the declared subset boundary into a discoverable fact, the exact diagnosability shape objectstack#6936 spent a card on. (A) is rejected here: it changes evaluation semantics with a regression path the card itself names (`data.type == text` unquoted-string usage flips to fail-open), and the semantic correction belongs to C/D. (C) the CEL replacement dissolves this card at M9 — the diagnostic carries a pointer so it retires with the file. (D) publish-time predicate validation is the objectstack-side contract half — the seat relays onto #6936's companion card once the dev locates its number from that thread.

**ACCEPT** (objectui seat PM, session `session_017Qqyix2QcnpUC9XeYVDzx3`, review of record) — PR #4264, CI fully green. Ruling B executed with zero semantic change, proven mechanically (every §7.3 zero-semantics pin green THROUGH the reverse-verification revert — the strongest form of the claim).

Two structural choices deserve the record. The diagnostic sits AT `parseLiteral`'s tail rather than at any call site, so every route to that line carries it — and the operator-coverage statement is measured, not asserted (the `in` branch's right side is proven unreachable by its own regex; `resolveValue`'s shortcut route is covered by construction and never identifier-shaped). The warning idiom mirrors #6936's landed `warnUnresolvedPath` in the same file exactly — channel, dev gate, warn-once memo keyed on the (text, predicate-source) pair, test hook extended — with the predicate source threaded down so the author sees THEIR expression named. **Q1 ruled: A, as shipped** — the identifier-chain grammar over my parenthetical's literal "contains a dot": a diagnostic that miscalls a malformed number a path is the noise that gets channels muted, and the narrowing is pinned with its reasoning in-code, one regex away if ever overturned. #4266 (the `in` array-parse collapsing the whole set on one bad element — a third silent-wrong-verdict path reachable by neither diagnostic) is graded `finding` correctly. **Q2 ruled: A — the seat is filing the fresh objectstack card now** extending the LANDED #7214 publish-time check (a closed completed card is the wrong place to accrete scope; the "right side is path-shaped" refusal is genuinely different from "path fails to resolve").
